body.html: I-Home Residence and Hotel overview — who it suits — to put it as briefly as possible, I-Home Residence and Hotel is a place for people who want "a clean, quiet, great-value base near the industrial estates" in Pluak Daeng, on the Chonburi-Rayong border · it isn't a beachfront resort that whisks you off to swim and relax, and it isn't a luxury city hotel selling its design · instead it's a residence and hotel with around 60 rooms on Soi Mapyangphon 25, near the Amata City and Eastern Seaboard estate clusters, built specifically around the lives of people working in the Eastern industrial zone · real reviews line up on this point: the people it suits are engineers, factory staff, contractors, and project teams who need to be on site in the estates for days or months, as well as anyone driving in to handle business around Pluak Daeng-Bo Win who wants a clean, quiet room on a reasonable budget · another group that finds it convenient is the families of staff who move in for the long term, since it's open for both daily and monthly stays and has serviced-apartment-style rooms that come fully furnished · for anyone hunting for a luxury resort with a big pool, a spa, or a full holiday atmosphere, this may not be the answer, because the main draw is cleanliness, quiet, a location near the estates, and value — not luxury.

Location and getting around — I-Home's biggest strength is sitting right in the Eastern industrial zone, in Pluak Daeng, on Soi Mapyangphon 25; the full address is 36/16 Moo 6, Map Yang Phon, Pluak Daeng, on the Chonburi-Rayong border · from the property it's just a few minutes' drive to the East's main estate clusters — the Amata City Rayong, Eastern Seaboard, Pinthong, and Hemaraj estates — which is the main reason workers choose to stay here, because you can wake up and reach the factory quickly without spending too long stuck in traffic on the main roads · for food and daily needs, the area around the property is a working-community neighborhood with a decent choice of made-to-order eateries, noodle shops, convenience stores, and markets · about a 15-minute drive gets you to Robinson Lifestyle Bo Win and Saphan Si market, which have supermarkets, restaurants, and shops to stock up the room or grab dinner · for weekend trips, the property is about a 30-40 min drive from Pattaya and within easy driving distance of Khao Kheow Open Zoo and attractions on the Chonburi-Rayong side · for longer journeys, it's a little over an hour from U-Tapao and Suvarnabhumi airports, and there's an airport transfer service (for an extra fee) · one thing that comes up in real reviews is that Pluak Daeng is a car-dependent area, not a neighborhood where you can easily walk around, so if you don't have your own car you should plan your travel and food ahead, and during the morning and evening rush when everyone is heading in and out of the estates the main roads get fairly busy — leave extra time.

"The room was very clean, the AC was icy cold, and it was nice and quiet for a good night's sleep — perfect for coming in to work in the estate and then coming back to actually rest · there's an on-site restaurant and convenience store, so at night you don't have to drive far, and the parking is free too. Great value for just a few hundred baht."

Room types and decor — I-Home is a residence with several room types to choose from by size and number of guests · it starts with standard rooms like the Standard Queen and Standard Triple at around 22 sqm, compact but laid out well, good for solo travelers or two people coming in for work, with the Standard Triple adding a single bed that suits teams traveling together · stepping up, there's the Superior Queen and Superior Twin for those who want a more comfortable room, and the largest is the Premier King at around 44 sqm, which gives you plenty of space for a long stay or a small family · every room has AC, a fridge, a work desk, an LCD TV with satellite channels, and a shower bathroom, and many have a private balcony to step out for some air · the decor is in a clean, simple residence style, focused on function over luxury, which fits the working clientele who want a clean room, a good night's sleep, and a work desk · the highlight reviews mention most often is the cleanliness of the rooms and AC that's genuinely cold, along with the quiet that lets you sleep soundly — the things workers care about most · for monthly guests, the serviced-apartment-style rooms come fully furnished and suit long stays · to be straight with you, some reviews note that certain rooms don't have a hair dryer or a kettle and that the amenities can vary from room to room, so if you need these, ask or specify when booking, and packing your own to be safe is the smarter move.

Facilities, restaurant, and fitness — although I-Home doesn't have a pool, the facilities it does have line up neatly with what estate workers need · the highlight people mention is the on-site restaurant and convenience store, which means at night or late after work you don't have to drive far to find food or daily essentials — a big help in car-dependent Pluak Daeng · there's also a fitness room, a garden, and a terrace to sit and unwind after work, with an overall quiet, restful atmosphere · for basic services there's free Wi-Fi throughout, free parking, laundry service and coin-operated washing machines, a 24-hour front desk, and a 24-hour security system — and that last point earns high marks from long-stay guests and anyone who has to park overnight, since it brings peace of mind about the safety of both people and cars · there's also an information counter and an airport transfer service (for an extra fee) for those flying in for work · to be honest, the facilities here are at a "complete and genuinely usable" level for a working stay, rather than the resort kind with a pool, a spa, and leisure activities — but for a stay near the estates at this price, getting an on-site restaurant, a convenience store, a fitness room, and free parking with 24-hour security counts as plenty for a worker.

Food and dining — the property has its own restaurant open to guests, and a number of reviews praise the food as tasty and convenient — no need to head out on a night when you're worn out from work or it's raining, which is something estate workers value, since many get back late and don't want to drive far again · it's backed up by the on-site convenience store, which has food and daily essentials to buy any time · for other meals, the Pluak Daeng area has made-to-order eateries, noodle shops, and Isan restaurants nearby within a short drive, and if you want more choice you can drive over to Robinson Bo Win or Saphan Si market, which have both restaurants and supermarkets · what helps long-stay guests is that the rooms have a fridge, and the serviced-apartment-style rooms suit buying groceries to cook for yourself, which saves on food costs over many days or months · overall, food at I-Home is a convenient add-on that fits the lifestyle of estate workers well, rather than being a selling point like a luxury hotel's dining room — but in the context of a stay near the estates, having an on-site restaurant and convenience store is a clear advantage.

Service — service is a point that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews, especially the friendliness and willingness of the staff to help, with many saying they look after guests well and handle check-in and check-out quickly · there's a 24-hour front desk on hand, which matters a lot for shift workers or anyone arriving late · the overall atmosphere is quiet and orderly, the kind you get at a place whose regulars are estate workers, which makes it feel safe and comfortable · the team also helps with travel information, parking, and arranging monthly stays for those who need to stay long-term · to be straight with you, since this is a smaller property and not an international chain hotel, some extra services — like round-the-clock room service or a full concierge — may not be as complete as at a big hotel, and English communication can sometimes take a little patience on both sides, especially with international guests, but in terms of sincerity and attentiveness it's a real strength that lines up with the solid review scores.

Voices from real reviews (praise and gripes) — pulling together Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda, and Expedia, the picture is fairly positive · on the praise side: very clean rooms, genuinely cold AC, quiet and easy to sleep in, perfect for coming in to work in the estate and then coming back to rest; a location near the Amata City and Eastern Seaboard estates with a quick drive to the factory; an on-site restaurant and convenience store that make food and essentials easy; free parking with 24-hour security; friendly, helpful staff; and great value in the high-hundreds to low-thousands range · on the gripes side: what comes up is that some rooms don't have a hair dryer or a kettle, so you have to bring your own or ask first; some reviews note that bed firmness or the TV in certain rooms can be inconsistent; the Pluak Daeng area is car-dependent and isn't a neighborhood for walking around; and there's no pool for those who want a resort-style break · most of these gripes are about setting your expectations to match "a great-value stay near the estates for workers" rather than being major problems that keep people from coming back, which is reflected in review scores in the range of roughly 7.4-8.9 across several platforms, with Trip.com at around 8.9 from 84 reviews.

"I come several times a month for work in the estate, and what wins me over is that the room is always clean, the AC is cold, it's quiet, and parking is easy with security · the only gripe is that the room I got the first time had no kettle, so on later visits I asked ahead and the staff sorted it out for me."

Price and value — the starting rate for a standard room is about THB 680/night in the normal range, averaging around THB 700-1,000/night depending on room size and the season, while bigger rooms like the 44-sqm Premier King go higher with the size · for those who have to stay long-term, there's a monthly rate starting at around 5,000 baht, which is far better value than paying nightly and suits engineers or staff posted to a project for several months · compared with other stays near the estates around Pluak Daeng-Bo Win, I-Home feels very good value on cleanliness, quiet, and location, since you get a clean room with cold AC, an on-site restaurant, free parking, and 24-hour security in the high-hundreds to low-thousands range · compared with chain hotels like Hop Inn or big-brand serviced apartments in the Amata area that cost more, I-Home is the choice that emphasizes value and function for workers over brand and design · the trade-off is no pool and no resort-style facilities, but if you're here to work in the estate and want a clean, quiet room on a tight budget, especially for a long stay, every baht you pay earns its keep.

What to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if you need a hair dryer or a kettle, ask or specify when booking, because some rooms don't have them, and packing your own to be safe is the smarter move · two, if you're staying for several months to work in the estate, ask about the monthly rate directly, which is far better value than paying nightly, and check that the room you get is a serviced-apartment type with a fridge and full furnishings · three, on getting around — Pluak Daeng is car-dependent, so if you don't have your own car you should plan ahead for travel to the estate and finding food, and ask about the airport transfer service (for an extra fee) in advance · four, during the morning and evening rush when everyone is heading in and out of the estates the main roads get busy, so if you have to start work early, leave extra time · five, the address is in Pluak Daeng, on the Chonburi-Rayong border, so when you book or call a car, go by the Soi Mapyangphon 25, Map Yang Phon, Pluak Daeng address to avoid getting lost, and it's worth comparing prices across several platforms and choosing a free-cancellation option in advance if your plans are still uncertain.

The verdict — from all the real reviews, I-Home Residence and Hotel is the best fit for anyone who wants a clean, quiet, great-value base near the industrial estates in Pluak Daeng — whether that's engineers, factory staff, contractors, and project teams who need to be on site in the Amata City and Eastern Seaboard estates for days or months, or people driving in to handle business around Pluak Daeng-Bo Win who want a clean, quiet room on a reasonable budget · clean rooms with cold AC, an on-site restaurant, a convenience store, a fitness room, free parking, 24-hour security, plus the option of both daily and monthly stays, make it good value in an area where finding a rival at the same price isn't easy · if you're looking for a luxury resort with a pool and a spa, or want a stay in a walkable neighborhood, this one calls for an open mind, because the draw is cleanliness, quiet, a location near the estates, and value — not luxury · but for coming in to work in the Eastern industrial zone and wanting a clean, quiet room, a sound sleep, and value for every baht alongside attentive service — I-Home is a choice that meets that need well, and it's the reason it has consistently earned solid review scores from real guests.
